course.title: Grilling and Barbecue
course.tagline: Grill suya, chicken and fish over open fire with marinades people remember.

days.title: Grilling Basics: Your Grill and Tools
days.goal: Know your grill, your tools, and the safety rules.

video.title: The Most Succulent Grilled Chicken (Suya)

steps: Learn the two main grills: charcoal (uses coal) and gas (uses gas).
Find your tools: long tongs, a brush, a tray, and gloves.
Grill outside only. Never grill inside a room.
Keep water or a spray bottle nearby for small flare-ups.
Clean the grill grate with a brush before and after cooking.
days.task: Clean your grill and lay out your tools.
days.challenge: Light your grill and let it heat for 15 minutes with no food on it.

quiz.q: Why grill outside only?
options: Grills make smoke and fire that are not safe inside
quiz.explain: Grills make smoke and carbon monoxide. They are only safe outside.

quiz.q: What are long tongs for?
options: Turning hot food without burning your hands
quiz.explain: Long tongs keep your hands far from the heat.

quiz.q: Why clean the grate before cooking?
options: Old food sticks and burns, and makes new food stick
quiz.explain: A clean grate stops food sticking and tasting burnt.

days.title: Lighting Charcoal the Safe Way
days.goal: Light a charcoal grill with a chimney starter.

video.title: Nigerian Suya Recipe

steps: A chimney starter is a metal tube that lights coal fast and safely.
Fill the chimney with charcoal.
Put paper or fire starters under it and light them.
Wait 15 to 20 minutes until the coals are grey with ash.
Pour the coals out and spread them on one side of the grill.
days.task: Light your charcoal grill with a chimney starter.
days.challenge: Time how long your coals take to turn grey.

quiz.q: What is a chimney starter?
options: A metal tube that lights charcoal fast and safely
quiz.explain: A chimney starter lights coal quickly without lighter fluid.

quiz.q: How do you know coals are ready?
options: They are covered in grey ash
quiz.explain: Grey ash on the coals means they are hot and ready.

quiz.q: Why not use lighter fluid on food?
options: It can leave a chemical taste on the food
quiz.explain: Lighter fluid can leave a bad taste on your food.

days.title: Hot and Cool Zones: The Two-Zone Fire
days.goal: Set up a hot zone and a cool zone on your grill.

video.title: Chicken Suya

steps: A hot zone is where the coals are. It is for searing (fast, hot cooking).
A cool zone has no coals. It is for slow, gentle cooking.
Push all the coals to one side to make the two zones.
Sear food over the hot zone, then move it to the cool zone to finish.
Close the lid to cook with heat all around, like an oven.
days.task: Set up a two-zone fire and grill one piece of chicken.
days.challenge: Move the chicken from hot to cool zone and note the difference.

quiz.q: What is a hot zone?
options: The side with the coals, for fast hot cooking
quiz.explain: The hot zone is where the coals are. It sears food fast.

quiz.q: What is a cool zone for?
options: Slow, gentle cooking to finish food
quiz.explain: The cool zone finishes food gently without burning it.

quiz.q: Why close the lid?
options: It turns the grill into an oven and cooks food all around
quiz.explain: A closed lid traps heat so food cooks from all sides.

days.title: Suya Spice (Yaji): Make Your Own
days.goal: Make suya spice from scratch.

video.title: Beef Suya

steps: Yaji is the spicy peanut mix rubbed on suya.
Grind roasted peanuts into a coarse powder.
Add ginger powder, paprika, chilli powder, and salt.
Add a little garlic powder and onion powder if you have them.
Taste it. Add more chilli if you want it hotter. Store in a sealed jar.
days.task: Make a jar of suya spice.
days.challenge: Taste your spice on grilled chicken and adjust it.

quiz.q: What is yaji made from?
options: Ground peanuts with ginger, paprika, and chilli
quiz.explain: Yaji is built on ground peanuts with ginger, paprika, and chilli.

quiz.q: Why grind peanuts coarse, not smooth?
options: Coarse peanuts give suya its rough, crunchy coating
quiz.explain: Coarse ground peanuts coat the meat and give suya its texture.

quiz.q: How should you store yaji?
options: In a sealed jar, in a cool dry place
quiz.explain: A sealed jar keeps the spice dry and fresh.

days.title: Beef Suya: Thin Slices, Big Flavour
days.goal: Grill beef suya at home.

video.title: How to Grill (Almost) Everything

steps: Cut beef into thin, flat slices. Thin slices cook fast.
Rub the beef with oil, then coat it with suya spice.
Thread the slices onto skewers, flat, not bunched up.
Grill over medium heat. Turn often.
Brush with oil while grilling so it stays moist.
days.task: Grill beef suya.
days.challenge: Serve with sliced onion and extra suya spice.

quiz.q: Why cut suya meat thinly?
options: Thin slices cook fast and take on more spice
It is easier to chew only
quiz.explain: Thin slices grill quickly and carry more spice on their surface.

quiz.q: Why thread suya flat on skewers?
quiz.explain: Flat slices cook evenly. Bunched meat stays raw inside.

quiz.q: Why brush suya with oil while grilling?
quiz.explain: Oil stops the thin meat drying out over the fire.

days.title: Chicken Suya: Juicy Every Time
days.goal: Grill chicken suya that stays juicy.

video.title: How To Make Perfect Spatchcock Chicken On A Pellet Grill | Crispy Skin And Juicy Chicken Every Time

steps: Use chicken thighs or breast. Cut into thin strips.
Marinate means soak the meat in spice and oil for at least 30 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill over medium heat.
Turn every 2 minutes so it cooks evenly.
Check the inside: it must be white all the way through, not pink.
days.task: Grill chicken suya.
days.challenge: Marinate a second batch for 2 hours and compare the flavour.

quiz.q: What does 'marinate' mean?
options: To soak meat in spice and oil before cooking
quiz.explain: Marinating soaks meat in flavour before it hits the grill.

quiz.q: Why turn chicken suya every 2 minutes?
options: So it cooks evenly and does not burn
quiz.explain: Thin strips burn fast. Turning often keeps them even.

quiz.q: How do you know chicken is done?
options: The inside is white all the way through, not pink
quiz.explain: Chicken must be white inside, not pink, to be safe to eat.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Suya Night
days.goal: Grill beef and chicken suya for your household.

video.title: The Perfect Marinade for BBQ Ribs

steps: Make a fresh jar of suya spice.
Cut and marinate beef and chicken.
Light the grill and set up a hot zone and a cool zone.
Grill the chicken first, then the beef.
Serve with onion, cabbage, and extra spice.
days.task: Host a suya night for your household.
days.challenge: Ask everyone which suya they liked best and why.

quiz.q: Why grill chicken before beef?
options: Chicken takes longer and needs more care
quiz.explain: Chicken needs full cooking, so it goes on first.

quiz.q: What should you serve with suya?
options: Sliced onion and cabbage with extra spice
quiz.explain: Onion and cabbage with extra yaji are the classic suya partners.

quiz.q: Why make your own suya spice?
options: You control the heat and flavour
quiz.explain: Your own spice lets you set the heat and taste you want.

project.title: Host a Suya Night
project.brief: Grill beef and chicken suya with homemade spice for your household.
checks: Suya spice made from scratch
Beef cut thin and grilled evenly
Chicken cooked white all the way through
Grill set up with hot and cool zones
Served with onion, cabbage, and extra spice
Feedback collected from the people who ate

days.title: Grilled Chicken: The Whole Bird
days.goal: Grill a whole chicken so it stays juicy.

video.title: How Do I Prepare Ribs Before Grilling?

steps: Flatten the chicken by removing the backbone. This is called spatchcock.
A flat chicken cooks evenly and faster.
Rub it with oil, salt, and your favourite spice.
Grill skin side down over medium heat, then turn.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting so the juices stay in.
days.task: Grill a whole flattened chicken.
days.challenge: Cut it into 8 pieces and serve it.

quiz.q: What is spatchcock?
options: Removing the backbone so the chicken lies flat
quiz.explain: Spatchcock means the backbone is removed so the bird lies flat.

quiz.q: Why flatten a whole chicken?
quiz.explain: A flat chicken cooks at the same speed all over.

quiz.q: Why rest chicken before cutting?
options: Juices spread back through the meat so it stays moist
quiz.explain: Cutting at once lets the juices run out. Resting keeps them in.

days.title: Grilled Fish: Skin On, No Sticking
days.goal: Grill fish without it sticking or falling apart.

video.title: How to Use a Charcoal Grill Like a Pro

steps: Use firm fish like croaker, tilapia, or catfish.
Pat the fish dry. Wet fish sticks to the grill.
Rub with oil and spice. Oil the grill grate too.
Grill skin side down first. Do not move it until it releases.
Turn once only, then cook until the flesh flakes easily.
days.task: Grill a whole fish.
days.challenge: Grill fish fillets and compare how they behave.

quiz.q: Why pat fish dry before grilling?
options: Wet fish sticks to the grill
quiz.explain: Dry fish and an oiled grate stop sticking.

quiz.q: Why not move fish until it releases?
options: Fish lets go when the skin is crisp. Moving it early tears it
quiz.explain: Fish sticks at first, then releases when the skin crisps.

quiz.q: How do you know grilled fish is done?
options: The flesh flakes easily with a fork
quiz.explain: Cooked fish flakes apart easily with a fork.

days.title: BBQ Ribs: Prep and Marinade
days.goal: Prep ribs and make a marinade that works.

video.title: How to Start (And Put Out) a Charcoal Grill

steps: A marinade is a mix of oil, spice, and something sour that soaks into meat.
Remove the thin membrane from the back of the ribs.
Rub the ribs with salt, pepper, paprika, and garlic.
Pour over a little oil and lemon juice. Leave for at least 1 hour.
Keep the ribs in the fridge while they marinate.
days.task: Prep and marinate a rack of ribs.
days.challenge: Marinate a second rack overnight and compare the flavour.

quiz.q: What is a marinade?
options: A mix that soaks into meat to add flavour
quiz.explain: A marinade soaks into meat and adds flavour before cooking.

quiz.q: Why remove the membrane from ribs?
options: It stops flavour getting in and makes ribs tough
quiz.explain: The membrane blocks flavour and stays tough when cooked.

quiz.q: Why marinate in the fridge?
options: Meat left out warm can grow germs
quiz.explain: Raw meat must stay cold while it marinates.

days.title: Grilling Ribs Low and Slow
days.goal: Grill ribs low and slow until tender.

video.title: How to Light a Charcoal BBQ with or without a chimney starter

steps: Set up a cool zone with few coals. Ribs need gentle heat.
Place ribs on the cool side and close the lid.
Cook for 1 to 2 hours, turning every 30 minutes.
Brush with BBQ sauce in the last 20 minutes only.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
days.task: Grill ribs low and slow.
days.challenge: Brush with sauce at the end and taste the difference.

quiz.q: Why cook ribs on the cool side?
options: Gentle heat makes tough ribs tender
quiz.explain: Low, slow heat breaks down tough meat and makes it tender.

quiz.q: Why add BBQ sauce only at the end?
options: Sauce burns if it cooks too long
quiz.explain: Sugar in BBQ sauce burns over long cooking, so it goes on last.

quiz.q: How do you know ribs are done?
options: The meat pulls back from the bone and feels tender
quiz.explain: Meat pulling back from the bone shows ribs are tender.

days.title: Grilled Burgers: Juicy Patties
days.goal: Grill burgers that stay juicy inside.

video.title: The Most Succulent Grilled Chicken (Suya)

steps: Use beef with some fat in it. Very lean beef makes dry burgers.
Shape patties gently. Do not press them too hard.
Make a small dent in the middle so they cook flat.
Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes each side.
Do not press the burger down. Pressing pushes the juices out.
days.task: Grill burgers for your household.
days.challenge: Add cheese in the last minute and let it melt.

quiz.q: Why use beef with fat for burgers?
quiz.explain: Fat melts as the burger cooks and keeps it moist.

quiz.q: Why make a dent in the middle?
options: So the burger cooks flat instead of puffing up
quiz.explain: Burgers puff up in the middle. A dent keeps them flat.

quiz.q: Why not press a burger down?
quiz.explain: Pressing squeezes the juice out and makes a dry burger.

days.title: Grilled Vegetables and Corn
days.goal: Grill vegetables and corn on the cob.

video.title: Nigerian Suya Recipe

steps: Cut vegetables thick so they do not fall through the grate.
Toss in oil and salt before grilling.
Grill corn in its husk or wrapped in foil.
Turn often. Vegetables burn fast.
Brush with butter and serve hot.
days.task: Grill a mix of vegetables and corn.
days.challenge: Grill plantain slices and serve them with the vegetables.

quiz.q: Why cut vegetables thick for grilling?
options: Thin pieces fall through the grate
quiz.explain: Thick pieces stay on the grill and cook evenly.

quiz.q: Why grill corn in its husk or foil?
options: It steams inside and stays moist
quiz.explain: Husk or foil traps steam so the corn stays juicy.

quiz.q: Why turn vegetables often?
options: They burn fast on a hot grill
quiz.explain: Vegetables are thin and burn quickly, so turn them often.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A BBQ Spread
days.goal: Grill a full BBQ spread for friends or family.

video.title: Chicken Suya

steps: Plan the menu: chicken, ribs, burgers, and vegetables.
Write a shopping list with costs.
Marinate the chicken and ribs the night before.
Grill in order: ribs first (slow), then chicken, then burgers.
Serve everything together with drinks.
days.task: Grill a BBQ spread for at least 4 people.
days.challenge: Cost the spread and work out the price per person.

quiz.q: Why marinate the night before?
quiz.explain: A long marinade soaks more flavour into the meat.

quiz.q: Why grill ribs first?
options: Ribs take the longest, so they start first
quiz.explain: Start with what takes longest so all food finishes together.

quiz.q: Why cost a BBQ spread?
options: So you know what to charge if you sell it
quiz.explain: Costing turns grilling into a business skill.

project.title: Grill a Full BBQ Spread
project.brief: Grill chicken, ribs, burgers, and vegetables for at least 4 people.
checks: Menu planned with costs per person
Chicken and ribs marinated in advance
Ribs cooked low and slow until tender
Burgers juicy, not pressed flat
Vegetables grilled and served hot
Spread served together and feedback collected

days.title: Grilling Safety and Clean-Up
days.goal: Grill safely and clean up properly.

video.title: Beef Suya

steps: Keep children and pets away from the grill.
Never leave a lit grill alone.
To put out charcoal, close the lid and all vents. The fire dies without air.
Let coals cool fully before throwing them away.
Brush the grate clean while it is still warm.
days.task: Do a full clean of your grill after cooking.
days.challenge: Practise putting out the coals safely.

quiz.q: How do you put out a charcoal grill?
options: Close the lid and vents so the fire dies without air
quiz.explain: Closing the lid and vents starves the fire of air.

quiz.q: Why clean the grate while it is warm?
quiz.explain: Warm grease wipes off. Cold grease sticks hard.

quiz.q: Why keep children away from the grill?
options: Grills are very hot and can burn
quiz.explain: A hot grill can cause bad burns in seconds.

days.title: Peppered Grilled Chicken
days.goal: Grill chicken with a pepper coating, party style.

video.title: How to Grill (Almost) Everything

steps: Grill chicken until cooked through.
Fry a thick pepper mix with onion until the oil separates.
Toss the grilled chicken in the pepper mix.
Cook on low for 5 minutes so the pepper sticks.
Serve hot as a main or as small chops.
days.task: Make peppered grilled chicken.
days.challenge: Make a second batch with more pepper and compare.

quiz.q: Why grill the chicken first?
options: So the pepper coats cooked chicken instead of stewing raw meat
quiz.explain: Pre-cooked chicken takes the pepper sauce without overcooking.

quiz.q: What makes a pepper mix thick enough to coat?
options: Frying it down until most water is gone
quiz.explain: A well-fried, thick pepper mix clings to meat.

quiz.q: What is peppered chicken often served as?
quiz.explain: Peppered chicken is a classic party small chop.

days.title: Grilled Turkey and Gizzard
days.goal: Grill turkey and gizzard for parties.

video.title: How To Make Perfect Spatchcock Chicken On A Pellet Grill | Crispy Skin And Juicy Chicken Every Time

steps: Boil gizzard with onion and seasoning until tender.
Grill the boiled gizzard for a smoky outside.
Cut turkey into pieces and marinate with spice and oil.
Grill over medium heat, turning often.
Serve with pepper sauce and onion.
days.task: Grill gizzard.
days.challenge: Grill turkey pieces the same way.

quiz.q: Why boil gizzard before grilling?
options: Gizzard is tough and needs boiling to soften
quiz.explain: Gizzard is tough. Boiling softens it before the grill adds flavour.

quiz.q: Why marinate turkey?
options: Marinade adds flavour and keeps it moist
quiz.explain: Marinade soaks flavour in and stops turkey drying out.

quiz.q: What goes well with grilled gizzard?
quiz.explain: Pepper sauce and onion are the classic partners.

days.title: BBQ Sauce from Scratch
days.goal: Make your own BBQ sauce.

video.title: The Perfect Marinade for BBQ Ribs

steps: Mix tomato paste, honey, vinegar, and a little chilli.
Add garlic powder, onion powder, and salt.
Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Taste it. Add more honey for sweet, more vinegar for sharp.
Cool and store in a sealed jar in the fridge.
days.task: Make a jar of BBQ sauce.
days.challenge: Use it on grilled chicken and compare with shop-bought sauce.

quiz.q: What gives BBQ sauce its sweet and sharp taste?
options: Honey for sweet and vinegar for sharp
quiz.explain: Honey makes it sweet. Vinegar makes it sharp.

quiz.q: Why simmer BBQ sauce?
quiz.explain: Simmering lets the flavours mix and the sauce thicken.

quiz.q: How long does homemade BBQ sauce keep?
quiz.explain: In a sealed jar in the fridge, it keeps about 2 weeks.

days.title: Grilling for a Crowd
days.goal: Grill for 10 or more people without stress.

video.title: How Do I Prepare Ribs Before Grilling?

steps: Plan the menu and write a shopping list.
Marinate everything the night before.
Grill in batches. Keep finished food warm in a low oven.
Ask a friend to help serve while you grill.
Keep a tray of food ready so guests never wait hungry.
days.task: Grill for a crowd of 10 or more, or plan it on paper.
days.challenge: Time your grilling and write down what took longest.

quiz.q: Why grill in batches?
quiz.explain: Too much food at once drops the heat and cooks unevenly.

quiz.q: How do you keep grilled food warm?
quiz.explain: A low oven keeps food warm without overcooking it.

quiz.q: Why ask a friend to help serve?
options: So you can stay at the grill while guests eat
quiz.explain: A helper lets you focus on grilling while guests are served.

days.title: Costing Grilled Food
days.goal: Work out what grilled food costs and what to charge.

video.title: How to Use a Charcoal Grill Like a Pro

steps: List every ingredient with its price, including charcoal.
Add the cost of skewers, foil, and packaging.
Divide the total by the number of portions.
Charge 2.5 to 3 times the food cost for a profit.
Compare with suya sellers near you.
days.task: Cost a plate of suya and set its selling price.
days.challenge: Cost a full BBQ plate the same way.

quiz.q: What costs must you count for grilling?
options: Meat, spice, charcoal, skewers, and packaging
quiz.explain: Charcoal, skewers, and packaging are real costs too.

quiz.q: Why charge 2.5 to 3 times the food cost?
options: To cover all costs and still make a profit
quiz.explain: The extra covers charcoal, packaging, your time, and profit.

quiz.q: Why compare with local suya sellers?
options: So your price is fair for your area
quiz.explain: Local prices tell you what customers expect to pay.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Grilled Feast
days.goal: Grill a full feast: suya, chicken, fish, and vegetables.

video.title: How to Start (And Put Out) a Charcoal Grill

steps: Choose the menu and write a shopping list with costs.
Make suya spice and BBQ sauce in advance.
Marinate everything the night before.
Grill in order: slow items first, fast items last.
Serve everything at once and photograph the table.
days.task: Grill a full feast for your household.
days.challenge: Serve it to a guest and ask for their favourite dish.

quiz.q: Why make spice and sauce in advance?
options: It frees up time on the grilling day
quiz.explain: Spice and sauce made early save time on the day.

quiz.q: What order do you grill in?
options: Slowest first, so all finish together
quiz.explain: Slow food starts first so everything is ready at once.

quiz.q: Why photograph your grilled food?
options: Photos track your progress and show customers later
quiz.explain: Photos record your work and become your portfolio if you sell food.

project.title: Grill a Full Feast
project.brief: Grill suya, chicken, fish, and vegetables, served together.
checks: Menu planned with costs
Spice and sauce made in advance
Suya grilled with homemade spice
Chicken cooked through and juicy
Fish grilled without sticking
Table photographed and feedback collected

days.title: Smoking on a Grill: The Easy Way
days.goal: Add smoke flavour to grilled food.

video.title: How to Light a Charcoal BBQ with or without a chimney starter

steps: Wood chips are small pieces of wood that make smoke.
Soak wood chips in water for 30 minutes.
Put them on the coals. They will smoke, not burn.
Close the lid so the smoke stays around the food.
Use a small handful. Too much smoke tastes bitter.
days.task: Smoke a piece of chicken on the grill.
days.challenge: Try smoking fish and compare the flavour.

quiz.q: What are wood chips?
options: Small pieces of wood that make smoke
quiz.explain: Wood chips burn slowly and make smoke that flavours food.

quiz.q: Why soak wood chips in water?
options: So they smoke instead of burning fast
quiz.explain: Wet chips smoulder and smoke. Dry chips burn up fast.

quiz.q: Why use only a small handful?
options: Too much smoke makes food taste bitter
quiz.explain: A little smoke adds flavour. Too much makes food bitter.

days.title: Grilled Sandwiches and Wraps
days.goal: Grill sandwiches and wraps for quick sales.

video.title: The Most Succulent Grilled Chicken (Suya)

steps: Fill bread or wraps with grilled chicken and vegetables.
Brush the outside with a little butter or oil.
Grill for 2 minutes each side until crisp and marked.
Cut in half and serve hot.
Add a simple sauce like pepper sauce or BBQ sauce.
days.task: Make grilled chicken sandwiches.
days.challenge: Make grilled wraps and compare which sells better with friends.

quiz.q: Why brush the outside of a sandwich?
options: It helps the bread crisp and brown
quiz.explain: Butter or oil on the outside makes the bread golden and crisp.

quiz.q: How long do grilled sandwiches take?
quiz.explain: Sandwiches are thin, so they grill in about 2 minutes per side.

quiz.q: Why cut sandwiches in half?
options: So people can see the filling and eat easily
quiz.explain: A cut sandwich shows the filling and is easy to hold.

days.title: Selling Grilled Food: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward selling grilled food.

video.title: Nigerian Suya Recipe

steps: Pick 2 or 3 items to sell: suya, grilled chicken, or burgers.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your grilled food in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you grill only what is sold.
days.task: Take photos of your best grilled food and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real order, even a small one, and deliver it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 2 or 3 items?
options: A small menu is easier to make well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

quiz.q: Why take orders in advance?
options: So you grill only what is sold and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

quiz.q: Why do photos matter?
options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell food.

days.title: Festive Grilling: Parties and Holidays
days.goal: Plan grilled food for a party or holiday.

video.title: Chicken Suya

steps: Plan the menu a week ahead.
Marinate meats and make sauces in advance.
Grill slow items first on the day.
Keep food warm in a low oven until serving.
Serve with drinks and take photos.
days.task: Plan a party grilling menu and grill one item from it.
days.challenge: Grill for a small party and time how long it takes.

quiz.q: Why marinate in advance for a party?
options: It saves time and adds more flavour
quiz.explain: Marinating early saves time on the party day and adds flavour.

quiz.q: What should you grill first at a party?
quiz.explain: Slow items start first so all food finishes together.

quiz.q: Why keep food warm in a low oven?
options: So guests always have hot food
quiz.explain: A low oven holds food hot without overcooking it.

days.title: Your Signature Grill Dish
days.goal: Choose and perfect one grilled dish you can make brilliantly.

video.title: Beef Suya

steps: Pick the dish your household loves most from this course.
Write the recipe in your own words with exact amounts.
Grill it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and grill it once more.
Get someone new to taste it and give honest feedback.
days.task: Grill your signature dish and write the final recipe down.
days.challenge: Grill it for someone new and record what they say.

quiz.q: What is a signature dish?
options: A dish you can grill brilliantly every time
A dish with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature dish is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe in your own words?
options: So you truly understand it and can repeat it
quiz.explain: Writing it yourself proves you understand each step.

quiz.q: Why get a new person to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite. New tasters are honest.

days.title: Keeping Records: Orders and Money
days.goal: Keep simple records of your grilling business.

video.title: How to Grill (Almost) Everything

steps: Write down every order: what, how many, who, and when.
Write down what you spent and what you earned.
Work out your profit each week.
Note which dishes sell best and which do not.
Keep your money for grilling separate from your spending money.
days.task: Start a simple order book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out your profit from one suya night.

quiz.q: Why write down every order?
options: So nothing is forgotten and you know what to grill
quiz.explain: Written orders stop mistakes and show what sells.

quiz.q: What is profit?
options: What is left after costs are taken from what you earned
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for meat, charcoal, and packaging.

quiz.q: Why keep grilling money separate?
options: So you always know if grilling is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true profit of your grilling.

days.title: Grilling in the Rain and Wind
days.goal: Grill well even when the weather is bad.

video.title: How To Make Perfect Spatchcock Chicken On A Pellet Grill | Crispy Skin And Juicy Chicken Every Time

steps: Wind makes coals burn faster. Use fewer coals on a windy day.
Keep the lid closed more to hold the heat in.
Move the grill to a sheltered spot, but never inside.
Rain cools the grill. Add a few more coals.
Wear gloves. Wet hands and hot grills are a bad mix.
days.task: Grill on a windy day and note what changes.
days.challenge: Write down three weather tips for your grilling notes.

quiz.q: Why does wind make coals burn faster?
options: Wind feeds the fire with air
quiz.explain: Wind gives the fire more air, so coals burn hotter and faster.

quiz.q: Why keep the lid closed in bad weather?
quiz.explain: A closed lid traps heat when wind and rain cool the grill.

quiz.q: Why never grill inside?
options: Grills make smoke and fire that are not safe inside
quiz.explain: Grills make smoke and carbon monoxide. They are only safe outside.

steps: Light a charcoal grill from memory, without help.

days.task: Grill a full meal from memory, no recipe.
days.challenge: Teach one grilling skill from this course to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What is a two-zone fire?
options: A hot side with coals and a cool side without
quiz.explain: Two zones mean a hot side for searing and a cool side for slow cooking.

quiz.q: What temperature must chicken reach?
quiz.explain: Chicken must reach 75°C inside to be safe.

quiz.q: Why teach a skill to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

options: Everything you learned: fire, spice, grilling, and costing

quiz.q: Why start with the slowest item?
options: So everything finishes at the same time
quiz.explain: Slow food starts first so all food is ready together.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real grill
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Grill Master's Feast: Suya, Chicken, Fish and More
capstone.brief: Grill a full feast for your household or customers: beef suya with homemade spice, grilled chicken, grilled fish, and grilled vegetables, with your own BBQ sauce. Cost the whole feast and serve everything hot at the same time.
checks: Menu planned with a shopping list and costs per person
Suya spice made from scratch
Beef suya thin, even, and well spiced
Chicken cooked through and juicy
Fish grilled without sticking or breaking
Vegetables grilled and served hot
Feedback collected from at least one person who ate
deliverables: A photo of the finished grill feast
Your written menu with the shopping list and costs
Your grilling order, starting with the slowest item
Your signature grill dish recipe written in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
